description: Nordlo Sentrumsløpet Haugesund is a fast, officially measured road race starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen in Haugesund. The event offers a 10 km race consisting of two 5 km laps, as well as a new 5 km race on the same route. It is suitable for all levels, from beginners to elite runners, and creates a festive atmosphere in the city centre with closed roads and lively crowds. A children’s race is also held for the youngest participants, and there are opportunities to socialise after the race.
course_highlights: The 10 km route passes through the pedestrian street in Haraldsgaten, around the city park and along Salhusvegen to Karmsund videregående skole
The 5 km route follows the same course as the 10 km race, but covers one lap
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen, with roads closed to traffic
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00 and covers approximately 500 m for ages 0–12. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The 5 km race starts at 12:00, the elite 10 km at 13:00 and the main 10 km field at 13:20. Pacers are available, and electronic timing includes gun time and split times. A water and squash station is provided halfway around the course. AfterRUN, with food and drinks for sale, takes place after the race. Race numbers can be collected in advance at Anton Sport Oasen or on race day at Rådhusplassen. Changing facilities and bag storage are available at the start/finish. Roads are closed to traffic during the race. The course is stated to be certified by World Athletics with an AIMS-B certificate. Roads are closed to traffic during the race.

name: Hamarløpet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: kr 250,- fra påmeldingsstart frem til og med 2. februar (Early Bird)

description: Hamarløpet is a 10-kilometre road race through some of the most beautiful areas of Hamar, along Lake Mjøsa and the city’s walking paths. The race is organised to promote public health and motivate both experienced runners and recreational runners to take part in an inclusive and active experience. Starting at Koigen, the route passes Ridehusstranda, Domkirkeodden and Strandveien, offering a lovely combination of urban and natural scenery. A free children’s race is also held for children up to 12 years old, with medals and entertainment. Hamarløpet is an ideal event where any surplus goes to charitable causes.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 10 km course along scenic walking paths by Lake Mjøsa
Passes Ridehusstranda, Domkirkeodden, Strandveien and two railway underpasses
Water station and split time at 5 km
additional: Children’s race for ages 0–12, with free registration at the start, two routes of approximately 400 m and 1,000 m, medals for all children and entertainment in the finish area. Race bib collection for the main race is on Friday 21 May and on race day from 11:00 to 12:15. The prize ceremony takes place shortly after runners finish, with a perpetual trophy for the top woman and man, as well as prizes for age-category winners and draw prizes.

name: Saudafjellet Maraton 2027
description: Saudafjellet Marathon 2027 takes place on Saturday, May 22, in Sauda, Rogaland. This unique race offers spectacular scenery across Saudafjellet, one of Norway’s most impressive mountain passes. Participants can choose between the marathon, half marathon, or Gruvemila, and every distance offers a memorable experience in beautiful surroundings. The race starts at 12:00, and everyone is welcome to enjoy a challenging and wonderful day of running.
course_highlights: Run across Saudafjellet, a spectacular mountain pass
Choose between the marathon, half marathon, and Gruvemila
Scenic surroundings in Sauda, Rogaland
additional: Tickets are sold through EQ Timing via the Aett platform. The event runs from 12:00 to 15:00. Aett offers simple registration and ticket sales administration, with the option to pay at the door. The start time is listed as 12:00. Registration is through EQ Timing, and the organizer has announced an early bird offer.

name: KK-mila
description: KKmila is a fun race in Oslo offering two distances, 5 km and 10 km, on a flat, easy-to-run course that showcases the city at its best. Thousands of participants come together for a running festival full of great atmosphere, achievement and energy. The route runs along the waterfront, through parks and urban areas, and past iconic places such as Aker Brygge and Bjørvika, offering a varied and memorable experience. The event also focuses on community and supporting charity through its partnership with Right To Play.
course_highlights: Flat, easy-to-run course along the waterfront and through the city's parks
Passes well-known areas such as Frognerkilen, Tjuvholmen, Aker Brygge and Bjørvika
Varied and memorable route with a maritime feel and modern architecture
additional: The 5 km starts at 12:00 and the 10 km at 14:00. The race has pacers, timing, changing rooms, showers and toilets. Participants receive a goodie bag and this year's medal. Bag storage and a warm-up before the start are available. The event also includes a social after-run dinner for companies and groups. The race supports the charity Right To Play, and one lucky winner will be drawn to win a trip to KKcamp in Portugal. The Heia class is untimed, and participants are ranked alphabetically.

name: 4625løpet 2027
description: The 4625 Run takes place on Flekkerøy, a gem at the edge of the open sea just outside Kristiansand. The race offers varied terrain with many beautiful viewpoints and is suitable for both beginners and elite runners. The course passes through idyllic Southern Norwegian gardens, over the iconic bridge at Skibbusundet, and along the archipelago with views of Oksøy Lighthouse. After crossing the finish line, runners can look forward to a medal, recognition and well-earned refreshments.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with Kodak-friendly viewpoints
Run across the bridge at Skibbusundet, one of the island’s most photographed spots
Views of Oksøy Lighthouse and the beautiful archipelago
additional: The children’s race starts at 10:15 and 10:30, with courses of approximately 300 metres and 1 km. Toilets and changing rooms are available at Flekkerøyhallen, and bag storage is provided in the start area. Electronic timing is used for the 4625 Run, with a minimum age of 11. A water and sports drink station is located about halfway along the course at Geitodden. All participants receive a medal and pizza from Pizzabakeren after the race. Parking is available at the sports facility. Race numbers are distributed on race day from 09:00 and must be worn visibly. Separate children’s race. The main race starts at 11:00.

name: Vassøy Backyard Ultra
location: Vassøy skole, Sørstrandveien 38, Vassøy, Stavanger, Norway
description: Vassøy Backyard Ultra is a popular running festival on the island of Vassøy, held annually in May since 2023. The race consists of 6.7 km laps that must be completed within one hour, with up to 12 laps (12 hours) available. Before each lap, participants can choose between two course options: a road course and a trail course, both starting and finishing at Vassøy School. The event has sold out several years in a row and offers a social and challenging experience for runners of all levels.
course_highlights: 6.7 km per lap, with a maximum of 12 laps (12 hours)
Two course options: road and trail, both finishing on the artificial turf field
Start and finish at Vassøy School, Sørstrandveien 38
additional: Registration opens in autumn 2026. The race sold out in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Participants choose their course before each lap. The event is organized by Vassøy Idrettslag, a small and friendly sports club in the heart of Vassøy. Starts at 10:00 at Vassøy School, Sørstrandveien 38. Maximum of 12 laps (12 hours). Registration for 2027 opens in autumn 2026.

name: Askøy på langs
organizer: Askøy Turlag, Askøy Orienteringslag og Ask Friidrett
description: Askøy på langs is a spectacular race running from south to north across Askøy, with distances of 16 km and 37.3 km. The event offers a wonderful running and walking experience across varied terrain, including the island’s highest point and dense forests. It starts at Kleppestø quay and finishes at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. Walking and running categories are available for both distances, with start times arranged to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers. The event prioritizes safety with first-aid equipment and clear course markings, and offers increased toilet capacity and photographers along the route for an enjoyable experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain crossing the island’s highest point
Course from Kleppestø to Herdla Museum
Start times arranged to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers
additional: The full distance starts at 08:00 from Kleppestø quay, and the half distance (16 km) starts at 12:00 from Træet School. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. Toilet capacity has been increased at Kleppestø quay and Træet, and lighting has been installed. Photographers are stationed along the route at marked locations and wear vests. The full distance starts at Kleppestø quay at 08:00, while the half distance starts at Træet School at 12:00. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. The course includes wet and muddy sections, trails, walking paths, and some stretches of asphalt.

name: Greifenstein Berglauf
organizer: Fussfit Petry GmbH, webconcept GbR, weitere lokale Sponsoren
description: The Greifenstein Mountain Run is a challenging 5.3 km road race from Ehringshausen-Katzenfurt to Greifenstein Castle, taking place for the 27th time. The route follows country roads and farm tracks, climbing a total of 260 metres to the finish at the castle, which offers a wonderful view of the region. The race is open to youth, men, women and seniors, with one combined ranking for all categories. Nordic walking is offered without age-group rankings, and a free Bambini run for the youngest participants takes place separately in the afternoon. The event concludes with an awards ceremony and refreshments in the courtyard of Greifenstein Castle.
course_highlights: 5.3 km road race with 260 metres of elevation gain
Start in Katzenfurt, finish at Greifenstein Castle with panoramic views
Challenging section of the course above Edingen
additional: The entry fee includes a bus transfer to the start, transport of clothing to the finish, and drinks at the start and finish. Race numbers and finisher shirts will be handed out in the courtyard of Greifenstein Castle on event day from 14:00. Late registration is available on event day until 30 minutes before the start. Parking is available at the edge of Greifenstein village in the direction of Beilstein. A free Bambini run for children is offered at approximately 16:50, accompanied by members of LG Dill. The awards ceremony and refreshments, including coffee, cake, cold drinks and bratwurst, take place in the castle courtyard. In clear weather, the courtyard offers an impressive view across the Dill Valley to the Feldberg in the Taunus.

name: Internationaler Biesfelder Dorflauf
location: Kürten, Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
price_range: 3,00 € Nachmeldegebühr ab 23.05.2026, sonst keine expliziten Preise genannt
description: The International Biesfeld Village Run is a long-standing running event in the municipality of Kürten. The race is known for its hilly course, which challenges runners, and its slogan, “Flat is somewhere else.” Various distances, including races for toddlers and schoolchildren, offer suitable competitions for all age groups. The event is organised by Biesfeld Triathlon e.V. and has a family-friendly atmosphere, with the start and finish at the Biesfeld Community Primary School.
course_highlights: A hilly race in the municipality of Kürten with challenging climbs
Distances from 0.6 km (toddlers’ race) to 9.2 km (main race)
Start and finish in the schoolyard of Biesfeld Community Primary School
additional: Race packs are handed out on race day in the schoolyard of Biesfeld Community Primary School. No separate timing chip is needed, as the chip is integrated into the race number (RaceResult). Distances: 0.6 km, 2.1 km, 9.2 km; race number with chip; event in Kürten-Biesfeld

name: Wälster Lauf
description: The Wälster Lauf is a traditional fun run and road race in Drensteinfurt-Walstedde, organized annually by Fortuna Walstedde. The course is measured by the German Athletics Association (DLV) and offers runners and walkers of all ages an appealing opportunity to take part in sport. The event traditionally opens Sports Week in the village of Walstedde, known as the Lambertusdorf, and continues to attract growing numbers of participants. Alongside competition, enjoyment of exercise and community are also central to the event.
course_highlights: DLV-measured course in Drensteinfurt-Walstedde
Fun run and road race with various distances
Traditional opening of Sports Week in the Lambertusdorf of Walstedde
additional: The Wälster Lauf offers running and walking on a DLV-measured course. The event includes various age groups and distances, including a Bambini run, schoolchildren’s races, a fun run, 5 km and 10 km road races, and walking. Start times are staggered from 15:30 to 17:15. The event is a well-established regional running tradition, with courses known for their accuracy and fairness. It is suitable for both recreational runners and competitive athletes.

name: Botaniczna Piątka Gdynia – edycja wiosenna 2026
location: Leśny Ogród Botaniczny Marszewo, Gdynia, Poland
description: Botaniczna Piątka Gdynia - Spring 2026 edition is a cross-country race held in the picturesque Marszewo Forest Botanical Garden in Gdynia. The event is part of the Botaniczna Piątka race series, which has been promoting running and the beauty of natural routes in Poland since 2014. The race attracts running enthusiasts who value being close to nature and the beauty of their surroundings. It’s a great opportunity to spend time outdoors among greenery and enjoy a unique atmosphere.
course_highlights: Cross-country route in the Marszewo Forest Botanical Garden
Picturesque natural surroundings and scenic beauty
Spring race as part of the Botaniczna Piątka series
additional: The race takes place between 10:00 and 14:00. The organizers are a group of running enthusiasts who focus on cross-country races and the scenic appeal of the locations. The event is part of a race series held in various cities across Poland during the spring season.

name: Bieg Lwa
location: Tarnowo Podgórne, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Lion Run is an annual half marathon held in Tarnowo Podgórne, attracting runners from across Poland. The route passes through scenic areas, offering participants both sporting challenges and beautiful views. The event is part of the Lion Festival, which also includes other races and additional attractions, such as an EXPO featuring partners and cheering competitions. The Lion Run is an excellent opportunity for sporting competition and socializing in a friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: The half-marathon route passes through Tarnowo Podgórne and includes refreshment stations
Scenic views and varied terrain
Organized as part of the Lion Festival, with additional attractions
additional: The event includes the Lion EXPO, with dozens of partner stands. The streets of Tarnowo Podgórne will be closed on race day from 17:00 to 23:00. A contest is being held in which every hundredth person wins prizes. Race and recovery packages are available for half-marathon participants.

name: Bieg Poznaniaka
description: Bieg Poznaniaka is an annual running event held in Szreniawa, surrounded by Wielkopolski National Park. The event includes main races over 11 km and 5.5 km, a Nordic Walking event, and numerous races for children and young people. The main race course follows a marked loop of approximately 5.5 km, which participants in the longer race complete twice. The event is organized by the Aperio Association, and its goal is to support the education of children and young people with autism.
course_highlights: The main race and Nordic Walking course follows a marked loop of approximately 5.5 km in Wielkopolski National Park
Participants in the 11 km race complete the loop twice; those in the 5.5 km race and Nordic Walking event complete it once
Children’s races take place at the National Museum of Agriculture and Agro-Food Industry in Szreniawa
additional: Race packets can be collected on race day at the National Museum of Agriculture and Agro-Food Industry in Szreniawa from 9:00 to 14:00. A bag drop is available at the venue. Participants are advised to arrive at least one hour before the start. A limited number of race packets (10) for the 11 km, 5.5 km, and Nordic Walking events will be available on race day; payment is cash only. Children’s races are divided into separate heats for the safety of the youngest participants. Participants aged 16–18 who are not accompanied by a guardian must have consent from a parent or legal guardian. The children’s awards ceremony will take place at around 12:25, and the adults’ awards ceremony at 14:45. The event ends at around 15:00.

name: Phoenix RUN
description: Phoenix RUN is a unique sporting event held in a picturesque forest near the Smolarnia forester’s lodge, close to Nowy Tomyśl. The event offers a variety of activities for the whole family, including a 10 km main race, 5 km nordic walking, and children’s races over distances from 100 to 800 metres. It’s a great opportunity to spend time actively surrounded by nature, regardless of sporting ability. The organizers provide generous race packs, healthy food, and a chillout zone, creating a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: 10 km main race in the forest near the Smolarnia forester’s lodge
5 km nordic walking for adults
Children’s races over distances from 100 to 800 m in age categories 3–15
additional: Start and finish by the Smolarnia forester’s lodge. Children’s races start at 9:00; the main race and adult nordic walking start at 11:00. The event takes place deep in the forest, offering the power of nature and a unique atmosphere. The organizers offer opportunities for participants to socialize, healthy and delicious food, and a chillout zone.

name: XXVIII Bieg Święców
description: The 28th Bieg Święców is an annual running event held in Sławno, commemorating important historical events and promoting physical activity. The 5 km main race runs through the municipal stadium, along a tartan track and on cycling paths, offering participants an attractive course. The event also includes children’s and youth races at the stadium, held on the tartan track. The organizers provide electronic timekeeping and a 45-minute time limit for finishing the race, ensuring safety and smooth organization.
course_highlights: Main race course: municipal stadium, tartan track, cycling paths (3 x 1.5 km)
Children’s and youth races at the municipal stadium — tartan track
Electronic timekeeping using the ChampionChip system
additional: The time limit for completing the main race is 45 minutes. Participants must follow the instructions of the judges and course marshals. The race is open to people aged 17 and over (born in 2009 or earlier). A medical certificate or a declaration stating that the participant is taking part at their own risk is required. Children and youth participating in their races must have permission signed by a legal guardian.

name: V Ultra Nordic Walking World Records
description: UltraWR is an international nordic walking event held in Na Skarpie Forest in Toruń. The festival features individual and team competitions in various events, as well as the open Ultra Nordic Walking Rally, which is ideal for people of all ages and ability levels. The rally route is 3 km long and runs along forest trails; participants can complete it multiple times during the four-hour event. The event promotes outdoor activity, community, competition, and care for the natural environment.
course_highlights: A 3 km rally route along the forest trails of Na Skarpie
Officially measured route with a chip that counts laps
Participants can complete the route multiple times over four hours
additional: The rally is free for children under 6, who will be registered on site. Participants receive a race bib and a chip for counting laps. A race pack and a recovery meal await participants. Visitors can tour the Bielawy Nursery Farm after registering in advance. The Dobrzejewice Forest District will run environmental and educational activities during the event. The rally is scheduled for Sunday, May 24, from 10:00 to 14:00. The fee depends on the number of people in the entry: from 20 zł for one person to 50 zł for five people; children under 6 can take part for free. The competition program includes 10 individual and team events.

name: Gerard Tebroke Memorialloop

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Inschrijven voor de GUV Businessrun : €125 per deelnemend team.

description: The Gerard Tebroke Memorial Run is an annual running event in Aalten offering various distances and categories, including kids’ runs, schoolchildren’s runs, business runs, and 5- and 10-kilometer races. The event takes place on Saturday, May 22, 2027, and offers a sporty, friendly atmosphere for runners of all ages and ability levels. Start times are spread throughout the afternoon and evening, allowing participants and spectators to enjoy a varied program.
course_highlights: Multiple race categories for all ages and ability levels
Location in the center of Aalten
Memorial run in honor of Gerard Tebroke
additional: Late registration for the 5- and 10-kilometer races is available at the registration desk at Markt 7, Aalten. Start times: 16:30 Het Noorden Kids’ Runs, 17:00 GUV Schoolchildren’s Run, 18:00 Sorba 5-Kilometer Run and GUV Business Run 5KM, 18:45 Ducona 10-Kilometer Run. The event is held every two years and has strong local and sporting significance.

name: Lustraløpet
price_range: Aktiv klasse: 250 kr + eventuell lisens; trimklasse: 150 kr; familie i trimklassen: 300 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmeldingsavgift aktiv klasse: kr. 250,-+ ev. lisens om du ikkje har heilårslisens.

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Påmeldingsavgift trimklasse familie kr. 300,- ( familie = føresette med born under 18 år)

description: Lustraløpet is a traditional 10 km road race on asphalt, starting at Neshøgdi and finishing at Luster oppvekstsenter. The race is held annually and is known for its beautiful scenery and excellent prizes made by local producers and artists. Great emphasis is placed on volunteer effort to ensure a successful event. In addition to the competitive class, there is a recreational class for those who want a social and scenic outing without timing.
course_highlights: 10 km road race on asphalt
Starts at Neshøgdi and finishes at Luster oppvekstsenter
Scenic surroundings and prizes featuring local art
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Nes/by the start no later than 13:45. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, but travelling by your own transport is recommended due to summer traffic. Changing rooms with showers are available in the finish area. The recreational class starts between 11:00 and 13:30. All participants receive free betasuppe (soup) with flatbread and cordial at the finish. A kiosk sells ice cream, soft drinks, lapper (Norwegian pancakes), betasuppe, cordial and hot dogs. Cash prizes are awarded for the sprint prize, best time and course record. The competitive class is for participants aged 13 and over. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, changing rooms with showers are available at the finish, and participants are served betasuppe with flatbread and cordial. Prices are based on the published information for 2026 and may change before the 2027 race.

name: Åsaneløpet 2027
price_range: 150–400 kr, i tillegg til lisens fra 13 år
description: Åsaneløpet is a long-standing recreational race in the heart of Åsane, Bergen, inviting the whole family to take part. The race offers 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as a children’s race where every child receives a medal and the first 800 participants receive a T-shirt. The event offers a welcoming race-day celebration with a warm-up, prize-giving, and activities such as a bouncy castle and face painting, and is suitable for both young and adult runners.
course_highlights: Run in the heart of Åsane with a lead bicycle in front of the runners
A 100-metre children’s race for the youngest participants, with a medal for everyone
Group warm-up with MOVA before the start
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts (for children only) can be collected from 11:00 on race day outside Building A at Thon Senter Åsane. The warm-up for the children’s race with MOVA starts at 11:45. The children’s race (approx. 100 m) starts at 12:00. Group warm-up with MOVA at 12:50. The 5 km and 10 km races start at 13:00, with a lead bicycle in front of the runners. Prize-giving and activities such as a bouncy castle, face painting, and athletics challenges take place after the race. Children below 3rd grade run 100 metres. There is a water station at the turnaround point on the 10 km course.

name: Jentebølgen - Oslo
description: Jentebølgen in Oslo is an inclusive public health race taking place on 23 May 2027. The race combines the joy of running with a strong focus on mental health, in partnership with Mental Helse Ungdom. Participants can enjoy a colourful Color Run with costumes, laughter and a mini-concert before the start, and everyone who finishes receives a medal. The event is open to all ages and ability levels, and welcomes walking, jogging and running on a 5–6 km course.
course_highlights: A 5–6 km course suitable for walking, jogging and running
A Color Run with colourful powder showers and costumes
A mini-concert before the start and a medal for all participants
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the venue two hours before the start or in advance to avoid queues. The course is accessible to people with disabilities, and companions can participate for free by presenting a companion certificate. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companies and sports clubs can register groups at special rates.

name: 23. Rintelner Volksbank-Lauf
description: Der Rintelner Volksbank-Lauf findet am 23. Mai 2027 in der historischen Altstadt von Rinteln statt. Die Laufstrecke führt durch die Altstadt und die Wallanlagen über Kopfsteinpflaster, asphaltierte Straßen und Gehwege. Es werden verschiedene Wettbewerbe für Kinder, Jugendliche und Erwachsene angeboten, darunter Bambini-Lauf, Schülerläufe, Walking, 5 km und 10 km Läufe. Die Veranstaltung ist familienfreundlich und bietet eine elektronische Zeitmessung mit Einweg-Chip. Die Vereinigte Turnerschaft Rinteln 1848 e.V. organisiert den Lauf und engagiert sich stark im Breiten- und Gesundheitssport in der Region.
course_highlights: Strecke durch die Rintelner Altstadt und Wallanlagen
Lauf über Kopfsteinpflaster, asphaltierte Straßen und Gehwege
5 km- und 10 km-Strecken sind DLV-vermessen und bestenlistenfähig
additional: Startnummernausgabe am Vortag von 17:00 bis 19:00 Uhr und am Wettkampftag bis 60 Minuten vor dem Start im Tourismusbüro Westliches Weserbergland. Zeitmessung erfolgt elektronisch mit Einweg-Chip in der Startnummer (RACE RESULT). Eigene Chips sind nicht zulässig. Das Tragen von Laufschuhen mit Dornen ist nicht erlaubt. Nachmeldungen sind mit einer Gebühr von 2 € möglich. Das Programm bietet Bambini- und Schülerläufe sowie Walking und Nordic Walking neben den Laufwettbewerben. Teilnehmende erhalten eine Erinnerungsmedaille.

name: Pi Lauf 2026
description: The Pi Run 2026 in Neunkirchen-Seelscheid offers a diverse range of races for all age groups and ability levels. The event includes distances ranging from Bambini and children’s races to a 13.4-kilometer main race, as well as walking. The course is scenic, with refreshment stations and good on-site facilities. Every finisher receives a medal, and the top runners are honored. The Lions Club will provide cakes and drinks.
course_highlights: 13.431 km main race with two refreshment stations at km 6.5 and 11.5
Short Bambini and children’s races (approx. 600 m and 1,100 m)
Refreshment station on the recreational race course at approx. 3 km
additional: Race number pickup is available from 08:00 on race day in the start/finish area or in the nearby school building. Late registration is possible until 60 minutes before each start, with a €2 late registration fee. Changing facilities and toilets are available in school buildings and nearby halls. There is ample parking nearby. Every finisher receives a medal, and Bambini runners can get a scoop of ice cream from the sponsor. Registration is through the Race Result platform; participants receive running shirts and a multifunctional scarf. The event takes place in typical temperatures of around 20°C.

name: Ra(h)ser-Run
description: The Ra(h)ser-Run is a flat race through the Rahser district of Viersen, with distances from 1 km to 10 km. The 5 km and 10 km courses are measured by the DLV and eligible for ranking lists, and run mostly along paved paths beside the Niers floodplains. The event offers races for different age groups, including a Bambini run for the youngest participants and a schools’ city championship. Timing is electronic, using transponders in the race bibs. Registration is online only; late registration is available until 60 minutes before the start.
course_highlights: Flat, paved loops through Rahser and along the Niers floodplains
The 5 km and 10 km courses are measured by the DLV and eligible for ranking lists
Kilometre markers and course marshals along the route
additional: Late registration is available until 60 minutes before each start for an additional fee of €5. Race bibs contain an integrated transponder for electronic timing, with both gun and net times. Sittarder Straße will be closed to through traffic between Kränkelsweg and Oberrahserstraße for the duration of the event. Participants can purchase an event T-shirt as part of online registration until 07.05. School and children’s races, free training sessions at Hoher Busch Stadium, race distances for different grade levels.

name: Spatzenberg-Lauf
description: The Spatzenberg Run is a traditional fun run in Löhne, following a hilly circular course around and over the Spatzenberg in the nature reserve. The route runs mostly on paved paths and roads and offers an attractive running opportunity for all age groups. In addition to the 9 km main race, there are shorter 6 km and 3 km races for schoolchildren. The event is organised by Turn- und Rasensportverein Löhne 1910 e.V., running group, and takes place at the Obernfeld sports field.
course_highlights: Hilly circular course around and over the Spatzenberg (nature reserve)
Route on paved paths and roads
Distances: 9 km, 6 km and 3 km schoolchildren’s race
additional: Timing is provided by a disposable chip attached to the back of the race bib. Race materials can be collected from 9:00 on the event day at the Obernfeld sports field. Late entries are possible on the event day until 10:15, while race bibs are available. Payment by SEPA direct debit for online registration or in cash when collecting race materials. Hilly course around the Spatzenberg, registration online or on the event day, timing with a disposable chip, water at the finish station

name: Sponsorenlauf Brustkrebshilfe Dorsten
location: Bürgerpark Maria Lindenhof, Dorsten, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
organizer: Khadijeh Mohri, Andreas Schilasky, Ali Abdali
description: The Sponsorship Run for Breast Cancer Support Dorsten is a charity event in Dorsten focused on supporting breast cancer services and raising awareness. It takes place in Bürgerpark Maria Lindenhof and offers various running and walking routes accessible to all ages and fitness levels. Alongside the sporting activities, supporting breast cancer services is the main focus. A minimum participation fee is charged, and participants can contribute additional donations. Participants can run, walk, or support the cause with a donation without taking part in the race.
course_highlights: Event in Bürgerpark Maria Lindenhof, with wide paths and plenty of green space
Distances: 800 m for children, 2.5 km and 5 km for running or walking
Accessible changing rooms and showers on site
additional: More than 2,000 participants are expected, with a fundraising goal of over 50,000 euros.

name: MAXiLauf 2026
organizer: Stadt Hamm, Amt für Konzernsteuerung und Sport
description: The MAXiLAUF in Hamm is an annual running event featuring flat, record-eligible courses that appeal to runners of all ability levels. Events include a half marathon, a 10 km run, a 5 km run, and children’s and toddlers’ races. The courses run through the city of Hamm and offer an attractive, approved circuit route passing many landmarks. All participants receive an exclusive medal, and trophies are awarded to the leading runners. The event is family-friendly and part of the Landesturnfest LTF26.
course_highlights: Flat, DLV-measured circuit courses through the city of Hamm
Courses eligible for inclusion in best lists
Attractive routes passing many landmarks
additional: Bib-number distribution from approx. 8:30 a.m. at the Stadtsportbund tent. Timing uses a race|result® chip attached to the bib. On-site registration is available. Cut-off times: half marathon 150 min, 10 km 90 min, 5 km 50 min. Personalised medal engraving can be booked for an additional fee. Certificates are available on-site and online. Official merchandise is available in the shop. The race features a DLV-measured circuit, medals for all finishers, online and on-site registration, and a festive atmosphere for runners and spectators.

name: 12 Bieg Elegant na 5
description: The 12th Elegant na 5 Run is an annual running event held in Mosina, scheduled for May 24 in 2026. The event offers a variety of distances for children, young people and people with disabilities, as well as a 5 km main race that runs through the streets of the Mosina municipality. The start and finish are at Plac 20 Października, and the main race begins at 11:15. Participants can choose a basic or extended package with a T-shirt, making the event appealing to a wide range of runners.

name: BoryRun
description: The event brings together sport, health and mindful time spent offline, promoting intergenerational inclusion and the joy of movement without the pressure of competition. The routes pass through the scenic Lower Silesian Forests and the historic grounds of Kliczków Castle, offering a chance to connect with nature and the region’s history. Children can take part in the special Boryrun Active race, featuring activities that develop fitness and confidence.

name: Gontyniec Ultra Trail
description: Gontyniec Ultra Trail is a mountain trail race held on the picturesque Gontyniec Hill in Chodzież, the highest elevation in the Greater Poland Lake District. The courses run mainly along forest trails marked with red and yellow signs, offering runners a variety of distances and elevation gains. Organized by the Gontyniec Ultra Trail Foundation, the event attracts cross-country and ultrarunning enthusiasts from across Poland, offering unique challenges over distances from 12 to 52 km. This iconic event combines sporting competition with the beauty of nature and the history of the region.

name: VI Niechanowska Dyszka i Piątka
description: The 6th Niechanowo 10K and 5K is an annual race held in the picturesque Planty Park in Niechanowo. The event offers two popular race distances: 10 km and 5 km, attracting both recreational and more experienced runners. It is an athletics event and a great opportunity to spend time outdoors in a friendly atmosphere. The organizers provide professional timekeeping and technical support.

name: XII Bieg z książką
description: The 12th Run with a Book, ON THE TRAIL TO THE FINISH, is an open running event organized by the Nicolaus Copernicus University Alumni Program and the NCUM Marathon Club. It is dedicated to the Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń community and to fans of running and reading. The race takes place on the university campus in Bielany, Toruń, and its route follows forest paths and lanes through the campus woodland. Participants must complete the course while holding a book weighing at least 100 grams, highlighting the event’s unique combination of sport and the promotion of reading. The race is sponsored by Robert Małecki, a crime fiction author and NCUM alumnus, who takes part in the race and meets participants after the competition.

name: Freedom Run Wageningen

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Het inschrijfgeld bedraagt € 15 en is hetzelfde voor alle afstanden.

description: The Freedom Run Wageningen is a running event that celebrates freedom and connection in the city of liberation. Organised by Lions Club Wageningen, participants run in support of Stichting Kind en Kans, which supports children from families with limited means. The run offers four distances and takes participants through beautiful natural areas and the city, mainly along paved cycle paths. Everyone is welcome to take part and contribute to a future in which no child is left on the sidelines.
course_highlights: Routes start at Visum Mundi in the Vrijheidskwartier
The 15 km and half marathon routes pass through natural areas and include approximately 90 metres of elevation gain
Finish with a scenic descent towards the finish at Visum Mundi
additional: Timing with a Race Result bib tag at the start/finish; an additional live intermediate timing point at 6 km for the 15k and 21k. A medal is available for €5. T-shirts can be ordered when registering. The organisers encourage sustainable transport and use sustainable materials, such as medals made from potato starch or waste wood and rPET cups at drink stations. Setting: city run; timing via bib tag; start/finish at Visum Mundi; parking near the start/finish; registration by advance entry only.

name: Liemerse Landloop

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Deelname voor de Kidsrun vanaf 4 jaar tot en met 12 jaar is kosteloos, nog wel even inschrijven.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Het inschrijfgeld bij de voorschrijving voor de 3 km is € 10,00.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Het inschrijfgeld bij de voorschrijving voor de 5 km is € 12,–.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Het inschrijfgeld bij de voorschrijving voor de 10 km is € 12,–.

description: The Liemerse Landloop is an annual running event held on the fourth Sunday in May in Oud-Zevenaar and Ooy. The course passes through picturesque villages and along the Liemerse dikes, with official certification for the 5 km and 10 km distances. Distances include 3 km, 5 km and 10 km, plus a free Kids’ Run for children up to 12 years old. The atmosphere is warm and festive, with strong volunteer involvement and a lovely keepsake for every participant.
course_highlights: Officially measured and certified 5 km and 10 km courses
Route through the countryside around Oud-Zevenaar and Ooy, along the Liemerse dikes
Start and finish at Koffiehuis Uniek, Kerkweg 10 in Oud-Zevenaar
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Saturday 30 May from 15:00 to 16:30 and on race day from 08:45 at Koffiehuis Uniek. Parking is available at Dijkweg and at the station, with shuttle buses running from 10:00. Prize-giving ceremonies take place after each distance on the terrace at the start/finish location. The Kids’ Run is divided into age groups, with distances of 500 and 1,000 metres. Teams of 3 to 5 people can take part in the 5 km. Registration is available online and on site; the event is run with the help of volunteers and offers various running categories.

name: Jentebølgen - Kristiansand
description: Jentebølgen in Kristiansand is an inclusive public health run taking place on 24 May 2027, with the start and finish at Tresse. The course is approximately 5 km long and suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog or run. The event focuses on community, a sense of achievement and mental health, and supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 per race entry sold. It is a colourful and lively experience with entertainment, medals for all participants, and the option to take part as a company or sports club.
course_highlights: Approximately 5 km course starting and finishing at Tresse, Kristiansand
Accessible course that also allows strollers
Colourful Color Run with costumes, a mini-concert and medals for everyone
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the event site two hours before the start, but collecting them in advance is recommended to avoid queues. Stands open one hour before the race, and entertainment begins 30–45 minutes before the start. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions can participate for free upon showing a companion certificate. There is no official timing, but participants can use their own watch. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. Race numbers can be collected at the event site on race day.

name: 01. Godelheimer See Marathon
description: The 1st Godelheimer See Marathon/Ultra in Höxter is taking place and is a premiere event with DUV recognition. The event gives runners the opportunity to experience a new route around Godelheimer See. The race is aimed at marathon and ultramarathon runners and promises a varied and challenging course in a natural setting. The organizer is 100 Marathon Club Deutschland, a club for experienced marathon runners.

name: Vårruset Jönköping
organizer: Marathongruppen med Hässelby SK och Spårvägens FK
description: Vårruset in Jönköping is part of Sweden’s largest fitness tour for women, where participants can run, jog or walk 2.5 or 5 km on a course measured for accuracy. The event is all about the joy of movement and togetherness, with a great atmosphere among women. Everyone who crosses the finish line receives a medal and a goody bag, and teams of five are treated to a picnic after finishing. It’s a festive spring evening with entertainment and encouragement along the course and at the event area by Lake Rocksjön in Knektaparken.
course_highlights: Accurately measured 5 km course
Two distances: 2.5 km and 5 km
Event area by Lake Rocksjön in Knektaparken
additional: You can opt out of timing when registering, in which case your result will not be published in the results list. The recommended age is 13 for 5 km and 11 for 2.5 km; younger participants are allowed when accompanied by an adult. Registration is binding and is open until one hour before the first start on race day. All participants who cross the finish line receive a medal and a goody bag.

name: Jentebølgen - Stavanger
description: Jentebølgen in Stavanger is an inclusive public health run held in collaboration with Mental Helse Ungdom. The course is between 5 and 6 kilometres long, and participants can walk, jog or run on accessible terrain. The event offers a colourful, uplifting experience with entertainment, a mini-concert before the start and a medal for everyone who finishes. Jentebølgen is more than a race — it is a place for people of all ages to connect through achievement, joy and community.
course_highlights: The course is 5–6 km long and accessible
Colour Run with colourful costumes and colour along the course
Mini-concert featuring young artists before the start
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the venue two hours before the start or in advance to avoid queues. Stalls open one hour before the race starts. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions can take part for free upon presentation of a companion certificate. All participants receive a medal. Companies and sports clubs can register groups using group tickets. Race bibs can be collected at the venue on race day. The venue for the 2027 event has not yet been announced.

name: Bolechowo na Sportowo
organizer: Centrum Rozwoju Kultury Fizycznej AKWEN w Czerwonaku
description: Bolechowo Sporty, or Active Czerwonak at Night, is a recurring, free sporting event organized by the Centre for the Development of Physical Culture in Czerwonak. The event takes place in the evening and combines physical activity with bringing the local community together. It is a long-standing tradition that attracts participants who want to spend time outdoors, running or walking in a friendly atmosphere.
additional: The event is free and takes place from 19:30 to 22:00. This evening sporting event is part of the Czerwonak Grand Prix series. There is no information about participant limits, fees, or start waves. Previous events have taken place in the evening; available results from one edition indicate a distance of 5 km.

name: Vårruset Karlstad
organizer: Vårruset i samarbete med IF Göta Karlstad
description: Vårruset in Karlstad is a popular spring running event offering a lovely, friendly running experience for women of all ages. The race follows a 5 km course, with both timed and untimed participation options. After the finish, teams of five are treated to a picnic, creating a pleasant opportunity to socialize. The event area is located between Sundstagymnasiet and Sundstabadet, and the organizer encourages participants to travel to the start in an environmentally friendly way.
course_highlights: 5 km course, timed or untimed
Start and finish in the area between Sundstagymnasiet and Sundstabadet
Picnic after the finish for teams of 5
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Intersport Bergvik in the days before the event and at the venue from 15:00 on race day. Race information is sent out about one week before the event. There is a supervised area where participants can leave their warm-up clothes before the start. The organizer recommends cycling or taking public transport to the event area. City buses are free upon presentation of a race bib or race information. Teams consist of 5 people and must be complete no later than one month before the event to receive picnic vouchers. Changing rooms are available at Sundsta Sports Hall. Teams registered with five people receive a picnic after the finish. Individual participants receive a medal, a finish-line bag, and a race bib.

name: Gladsheim Finspångs Stadslopp
description: Gladsheim Finspång City Race is an annual fun run through beautiful Finspång, starting and finishing in Bruksparken. The race offers a 7-kilometre course with smooth, even surfaces, ideal for both runners and recreational participants. For a shorter challenge, there is AktivRundan, approximately 3.8 kilometres with no timing, and children can take part in XL Bygg Lilla Slottsrundan, a 1.7-kilometre route through an easy-to-run park setting. All participants receive a medal and energy products, and there are great prizes to be won. The race is open to everyone, whether they walk, jog or run.
course_highlights: 7 km course with smooth, even surfaces through central Finspång
AktivRundan: 3.8 km without timing for walkers and joggers
XL Bygg Lilla Slottsrundan: 1.7 km for children through an easy-to-run park setting
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Stora Coop Finspång/Viberga on Tuesday, 26 May, between 15:00 and 19:00. Late registration is available at the bib collection point and at the start and finish area from 15:00 on race day. Timing uses a chip on the race bib tab; without it, no time will be recorded. The children’s race has four start times between 17:00 and 18:00, depending on age group. All participants receive a medal, energy products and a water bottle sponsored by local businesses. The children’s race prize-giving takes place on the stage in Bruksparken at 18:15. The race’s official website currently provides information about the 2026 edition; prices and practical details for 2027 have not been specified.

name: Jentebølgen - Bergen
description: Jentebølgen Bergen 2027 brings girls and women of all ages together for an afternoon filled with a sense of achievement, community and a great atmosphere. The event takes place on 26 May 2027 in Bergen and invites you to enjoy running and energy with friends, colleagues or family. The entry fee includes access to the race, insurance and ticket fee, creating a unique community at the starting line.
course_highlights: Course between 5 and 6 km
Participants can walk, jog or run
Accessible course for participants with disabilities
additional: The entry fee includes insurance and ticket fee. The event runs from 17:30 to 20:00. Participants are encouraged to take part with friends, colleagues or family for a social and energetic running experience. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The venue has not yet been announced.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Hovemoenløpet
description: Hovemoenløpet is a traditional race held in Lillehammer and is part of Sørdalskarusellen. The race starts and finishes by the Birdwatching Tower at Svarstadsletta, and follows pleasant gravel and woodland trails in the Hovemoen area. The course is approximately 4.2 km long following a recent route change due to road construction. The event includes both a mass start and a virtual race, and attracts many happy participants and spectators every year.
course_highlights: The course follows pleasant gravel and woodland trails in Hovemoen
Start and finish by the Birdwatching Tower at Svarstadsletta
The course is 4.2 km long following a route shortening due to road construction
additional: The mass start has one starting wave, beginning at 19:00. There is a water station in the finish area. First aid is provided by Lillehammer Red Cross Rescue Corps. A virtual race is held alongside the in-person event, with participants able to start whenever they want during the event period. Race bibs can be collected at the tent by the red artwork from 17:45. Prizes are awarded to the top man and woman and to all participants under 12. Virtual race times are recorded through self-reporting on My Page.

name: Jenteløpet Drammen
description: Jenteløpet Drammen, previously known as Jentebølgen Drammen, is a long-running race for girls, held annually since 1993 by IF Sturla Friidrett. The 5.5 km race follows the Drammenselva, starting and finishing at Bragernes torg. It is an inclusive event for all girls, whether they want to walk or run, and focuses on community and a great atmosphere. Proceeds from the race go to children’s sports at Sturla Friidrett, helping keep activities accessible to children and young people. There is a warm-up with MOVA before the start, and medals and prizes are awarded after the finish.
course_highlights: A flat, easy-to-run 5.5 km course along the Drammenselva
Start and finish at Bragernes torg in Drammen
Water station just past halfway at Landfalløybrua
additional: Race numbers can be picked up at Löplabbet Drammen at Engene 24 on the Tuesday before the race and on race day. Group warm-up with MOVA from the stage at 18:00. After the race, medals are awarded to all participants and prizes are drawn from the stage. Bag storage and toilets are available near the start/finish area. Public transport or walking from Drammen station, five minutes away, is recommended. Held on Wednesday, 26 May 2027. The warm-up with MOVA starts at 18:00, with the race starting at 18:30.

name: Sternchenlauf
description: The Sternchenlauf in Schloß Holte-Stukenbrock is a traditional fun run held annually on the Wednesday before Corpus Christi. The event offers various races for all age groups, from races for toddlers and children to 5 km and 10 km races, as well as walking. The course follows a varied 2.5 km loop with forest trails, gravel and asphalt, lined with enthusiastic spectators. In addition to individual categories, there are team and relay categories, making the race especially appealing to groups.
course_highlights: A varied 2.5 km loop with forest trails, gravel and asphalt
Flat course with clear signage
Out-and-back courses for the toddler, children’s and schoolchildren’s races on Falkenstraße
additional: Start times: toddler race 17:00, children’s race 17:15, 1.0 km schoolchildren’s race 17:30, 2.5 km schoolchildren’s race 17:45, 5 km race 18:30, 10 km race and 5 km walk 19:30. The walk starts at the same time as the 10 km race, at the back of the field. Participant limit: approximately 2,000; relays are limited to 50. Event shirts can be purchased during registration or on site. Changing rooms and showers are available. Start and finish at the Waldstadion Schwarz-Weiß Sende e.V. Registration is available for individual and group races. The 5 km race is fully booked; remaining places will be available on site from 16:00 on the day of the event. The event is part of the region’s running events and offers a welcoming, family atmosphere.

name: B2Run Hannover
description: B2Run Hannover is a corporate run covering a mostly flat route of around 6.5 km along the Maschsee, with a spectacular finish in the Heinz von Heiden Arena. The run is open to companies, organisations and individual participants from Hannover and the surrounding area, and promotes team spirit, motivation and a sense of community. The event features a professional supporting programme with hosting and music, and is ideal for beginners, walkers and experienced runners. The focus is on fun, togetherness and team building, not on personal bests.

name: Steglitzer Volkslauf
description: The Steglitz People’s Run is a traditional running event held at Lichterfelde Stadium in Berlin-Lichterfelde. Organized by TuS Lichterfelde von 1887 e.V., the event offers runners of all ages a sporting opportunity. It is known for its friendly atmosphere and well-organized event. The races start and finish at Lichterfelde Stadium, providing an attractive setting for participants and spectators.

name: S:t Hans Extreme
description:
The course winds around S:t Hans Backar in Lund. In the ultra classes, the goal is to run as many laps as possible in 6 hours. The 10 km runners complete 4 laps and the 5 km runners complete 2 laps. Extreme One runners complete one lap.

One lap is 2.55 km with 140 metres of elevation gain. This means 10.2 km and 560 m of elevation gain for the 10 km, and 5.1 km and 280 m of elevation gain for the 5 km. Each lap in the ultra classes is extended with a flat section where runners go out and back along the same route so they can cheer each other on. The ultra-class lap is 4.38 km in total.
course_highlights: The course runs through S:t Hans Backar: technical trail with clear climbs and descents
One lap is 2.55 km with 140 m of elevation gain (10 km = ~10.2 km, 560 m of elevation gain; 5 km = ~5.1 km, 280 m of elevation gain)
The ultra lap is 4.38 km, including an out-and-back section where runners can cheer each other on; ultra-class runners complete as many laps as possible in 6 hours
additional:
The ultra starts at 14:00; the other classes start from 17:45.
Registration is at 
https://mittlopp.se/Anmalan/Arrangemangsgrupp/SHE2027_1

name: Blodomloppet Örebro

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 13 maj – 26 maj: 400 kr (Lag: 2000 kr t.o.m. 26 maj)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 12 maj: 0 kr (upp till max 200 deltagare, därefter 100 kr)

description: Blodomloppet in Örebro is a recreational race that highlights the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes everyone to walk, jog or run with friends, family or colleagues. The event offers several distances, including 5 km, 10 km, the Special Race and Little Blodomloppet for children. It is a social, healthy activity that also promotes team spirit and wellness, with the option to participate in teams of five. After the race, participants often gather for a shared picnic, and the event area is well equipped for an enjoyable day for the whole family.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km courses for women and men
Special Race: approximately 2.1 km
Little Blodomloppet: approximately 750 m or 2.1 km for children aged 1–12
additional: You can register individually or in a team of five, with the option to fill vacant places later. Discounts are available for blood donors and ICA Stammis members (SEK 40), but not during late registration. There is no age limit for the 5 km and 10 km distances, but participants should be able to complete the course on their own or with an accompanying adult. Little Blodomloppet is for children aged 1–12, and adults may accompany them as long as they do not interfere with others. A large picnic is offered to participants after the race. Wellness allowances can be used when registering. The event takes place at Trängens IP. Participants receive, among other things, a T-shirt, race bib and medal; prices vary depending on the distance and registration date.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://blodomloppet.se/vara-lopp/orebro/): 2027-05-27 — "27 maj 2027" (was estimated 2027-06-01)

name: Vårruset
organizer: Marathongruppen, tillsammans med Hässelby SK, Spårvägens FK och lokal arrangör KFUM Örebro Friidrott
description: Vårruset in Örebro is a popular spring running event offering 2.5 km and 5 km distances on a measured course. The event is open to all ages. The recommended minimum age is 7 when accompanied by an adult for the shorter distance and 11 for the longer distance. Participants receive a medal, a finish-line bag and a race bib, and can opt for timing on the 5 km course. Teams that register are invited to a group picnic after finishing, making for a lovely social spring evening at Gustavsviksbadet. The event is all about community and fun, with activities and a music quiz for participants.
course_highlights: Measured 5 km course
Start and finish at Gustavsviksbadet
Water station and toilets in the event area
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Intersport Marieberg in the days before the event. Teams of 5 can enjoy a picnic after finishing. The event area is at Gustavsvik Camping, where parking is limited; participants are encouraged to travel in an environmentally friendly way. Participants are advised to change at home. A water station and toilets are available on site. There is an option to leave a bag of warm-up clothes labelled with your name and race number. Race information will be emailed approximately two weeks before the event. Timing is available as an optional extra for the 5 km. The recommended minimum age for the 2.5 km is 11, or 7 when accompanied by an adult; for the 5 km, it is 13, or 11 when accompanied by an adult.

name: Int. Volkslauf, 38. Int. Halbmarathon, 22. Walkinglauf
description: TV Schwafheim is hosting the 52nd International Fun Run, the 38th International Half Marathon, and the 22nd Walking Event in Moers-Schwafheim. Races for children, adults, and walkers range in distance from 500 m to the half marathon. The course is closed to traffic, with several aid stations and timing by the Race Result system. The event is family-friendly and welcomes local club runners as well as half-marathon runners looking for a community atmosphere.
course_highlights: Roads closed to traffic, with traffic rules to be observed
Several aid stations along the course
Timing with the Race Result system and two chips attached to the shoelaces
additional: Race number pickup in the morning at the clubhouse; late entries accepted until shortly before each start; showers at the clubhouse and in the Waldschule gym; certificates can be printed directly at the finish. Course maps, 2025 results, water stations, showers, registration from 08:00, late entries up to 30 minutes before the start, family-friendly

name: Klingenlauf
price_range: Erwachsene: 16,00 € bis 18,00 €, Jugendliche/Kinder: 8,00 €, Firmenstaffeln: 65,00 €, Staffeln: 10,00 €, Schul- und Gruppenstaffeln: 30,00 € bis 60,00 €
description: The Klingenlauf is a long-standing running event in Solingen, held in Südpark. With various events ranging from 1 km to 10 km, relay races, and a company run, the Klingenlauf offers suitable running options for all age groups and ability levels. The course runs through Solingen’s Südpark and along the Korkenziehertrasse. More than 1,500 runners take part each year, making the Klingenlauf a sporting highlight in the region.
course_highlights: Course through Solingen’s Südpark
Section along the Korkenziehertrasse
A variety of distances from 1 km to 10 km, as well as relay races
additional: Late registration is possible on the day of the event until 30 minutes before the respective start, provided the participant limit has not been reached. The late registration fee is €2.00. The 5 km run is divided into two races: Speed Run (max. 30 min.) at 18:15 and Fun Run (over 30 min.) at 18:45. Changing rooms, showers, and toilets are available on site. Various running categories, online registration, changing rooms, toilets, showers in the ice sports hall, limited baggage storage, certificates and honorary awards, award ceremonies at the event venue

name: Leihgesterner Volkslauf
description: The Leihgestern Fun Run takes place annually on Corpus Christi in the beautiful woodland landscape of Linden. The event offers runners and walkers a choice of a 5 km walk, a 5 km run, and a 10 km run. The courses run mostly on comfortable forest paths with moderate elevation changes and are suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Timing is done with a transponder, and race bibs require a deposit that is refunded when returned.
course_highlights: 5 km loop course with 95% forest paths and approximately 50 m of elevation gain
10 km loop course with 95% forest paths and approximately 110 m of elevation gain
A scenic route through the woodland landscape of Linden
additional: Race bib deposit of 2 EUR, refunded when the bib is returned. On-site registration is not possible. Gross and net times are recorded with a transponder. The start location is the TSG Leihgestern sports clubhouse, Waldstraße 32, 35440 Linden.

name: Leśna Piątka Pikuś
location: Parking Nadleśnictwa Karnieszewice, ul. Słupska, Koszalin, Poland

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Udział jest bezpłatny, zachęcamy do dobrowolnych wpłat wspierających organizację

description: Leśna Piątka Pikuś is an annual cross-country run held in Koszalin on the forest educational trail of the Karnieszewice Forest District. The route starts and finishes at the car park on Słupska Street and is open to participants of all ages and experience levels. There is no timing or racing; the event promotes recreation and spending time outdoors as a family. Participants are encouraged to wear fairytale costumes, creating a unique and welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: The route follows the forest educational trail of the Karnieszewice Forest District
Start and finish at the car park on Słupska Street in Koszalin
A recreational cross-country run with no timing
additional: Participation is open to everyone, regardless of age or ability. Participants are encouraged to dress in fairytale costumes, creating a unique atmosphere. On-site registration is also possible, but keepsakes and participation in the prize quiz are not guaranteed.

name: Eksjö Stadslopp
description: Eksjö Stadslopp is a community race that welcomes runners of all ages and ability levels. The race takes runners through the beautiful wooden town of Eksjö and offers an enjoyable running experience filled with energy, camaraderie and joy. The proceeds go to Eksjö Södra IK’s children’s and youth activities, so taking part also supports a good cause. The start and finish are at Stora Torget in Eksjö, and the event has a welcoming, inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race passes through one of Sweden’s most beautiful wooden towns
The course is available in several distances, including 10 km and a 5 km fun run
Start and finish at Stora Torget in Eksjö
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Snäckan next to the swimming pool. Changing facilities are available at Prästängshallen until 21:30 on race day. Start times vary by category, with children’s races starting from 18:00 onwards, the 10 km races for men and women starting at 19:30, and the 5 km fun run starting at 19:50. Group registration is available by email with invoicing. Results will be published on the club’s website after the race. The programme also includes a 1,000-metre youth race and a 600-metre children’s race.

name: Lindahls Helsingborg Night Run
description: Lindahls Helsingborg Night Run is a festive evening race that starts as the sun goes down at Gröningen in Helsingborg. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a fast, flat course along the city’s beautiful seafront promenade, with views of the sea. The race is all about joy, community and a spectator-friendly atmosphere, with music and a festive vibe. It’s a race for everyone, whether you want to run fast or enjoy running in the evening light.
course_highlights: A fast, flat course with only 2 metres of elevation gain per lap
The course follows Helsingborg’s seafront promenade, with views of the sea
The 10 km race consists of two laps, with a lap split at Gröningen where the crowd provides extra energy
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Löplabbet Helsingborg in the days before the race and at the venue from 20:00. Bag storage is available from 20:00 at the start and finish area. Löplabbet Pacers will be on hand to pace several finish times for both the 5 km and 10 km. An After Run party with food and drinks from partners takes place immediately after the finish. A maximum of 1500 participants for a high-quality event. Time limit: 90 minutes. Distance options are 5 km and 10 km.

name: Abendlauf Wilstedt bei Nacht
description: The Wilstedt Night Run takes place at night and transforms the village of Wilstedt into an atmospheric running course. The event is family-friendly and welcomes everyone, from beginners to experienced runners. The new route offers lovely views of the village at night. The atmosphere is rounded off by cheering spectators and an evening fireworks display.
course_highlights: New running route through Wilstedt with lovely views of the village
Atmospheric event with cheering spectators along the route
Floodlit swimming at Heidebad Wilstedt after the run until 22:30
additional: The start and finish are at the Wilstedt sports grounds. The event begins with the mini run at 20:15, followed by the jogging and walking starts. Late registrations are possible on the day of the event from 18:30 to 20:00; the entry fee is then 9 euros. T-shirts or technical shirts are available only to those who register in advance and will be handed out on the day of the event. After the run, floodlit swimming at Heidebad Wilstedt is free until 22:30. Fireworks bring the event to a close at around 22:45. Nordic walking poles are not permitted on the running route. Children’s buggies and running strollers are permitted only for hiking/walking. Shower and changing facilities are available to a limited extent. New running route through Wilstedt, family-friendly, in the evening, registration until 17 May, including a mini run, fireworks and musical entertainment.

name: Raesfelder Mai-Lauf
description: The Raesfeld May Run takes place annually on the last Friday in May and offers a varied running programme for all age groups. From the 400 m Bambini races for kindergarten children to the 5 km and 10 km races for adults, there is something for everyone. There is also a 5 km team run, encouraging the fun of running together. The 5 km and 10 km courses are measured by the German Athletics Association (DLV) and are therefore eligible for inclusion in rankings.
course_highlights: 400 m child-friendly course for Bambinis
1,000 m and 2.3 km courses for children and teenagers
5 km and 10 km courses for adults, measured by the DLV
additional: Start times: 16:00 Bambini races (400 m), 17:00 1,000 m schoolchildren’s race, 17:30 2.3 km schoolchildren’s race, 18:00 10 km Volksbank Run, 18:05 5 km walking race, 19:30 5 km company, family and team run. The 10 km course consists of two laps of the 5 km loop. Part of the Lippe-Issel Cup, registration required, family-friendly, various categories.

name: Lauf Rund um Burg
description: The 37th Run Around the Castle is part of the Cross and Forest Run Series and takes place around Burg in Dithmarschen. The event gives runners the opportunity to run scenic routes of 4.8 km and 10 km. The race is distinguished by its natural surroundings and varied course. Participants can look forward to a friendly atmosphere and a well-organized event.

name: Mühlhäuser Röblinglauf
description: The Mühlhäuser Röblinglauf is a charity run with the unique concept “Sport meets Music,” supporting the Mitteldeutschland Children’s Hospice. The event offers various races for children, teenagers, companies and individual runners, as well as walkers. Alongside the sporting event, there is musical entertainment and a KinderGarten concert, making the run a special experience for participants and spectators. Race materials can be collected the day before, and an AfterRöblinglauf Party takes place after the run.

name: Nacht von Hasbergen
description: The Night of Hasbergen is a traditional road race held in Hasbergen. The event offers exciting races for all age groups, from the Bambini run and relay race to the 10 km main race. The races take place on a new course, which was adapted due to construction work. The event begins with an opening ceremony and a show act for the Bambinis and ends with award ceremonies for the various competitions.

name: Kalkmineløbet 2027
distance_verbose: 52.7 km, Marathon, Halvmarathon, 10.54 km, 6 km, 2.5 km

name: Eventyrsport SkyTrail 2027 - powered by Kari Traa
Skatås ryggar
location: IFK Göteborg Orienterings klubb-anläggning, Skatås, Göteborg, Sweden
description: Skatås Ryggar is Gothenburg’s largest trail race, offering a fantastic trail-running experience on winding paths in the nature reserves around Skatås, the Delsjö area and Knipeflågsbergen. The race has several distances to suit everyone, from youth categories to a challenging half marathon over five ridges. The start and finish are at IFK Göteborg Orienteering’s clubhouse, and the courses are clearly marked to provide a safe and enjoyable running experience in a wilderness setting. All participants receive a wooden medal and have access to aid stations and good food after the race.
course_highlights: The course crosses five, four or two ridges in the Skatås and Delsjö area nature reserves
The longest course is 21.1 km and includes challenging terrain with rock slabs and winding paths
There are aid stations at four locations along the longest course, with sports drink and water
additional: Race bibs must be collected at the event venue before the start. The timing chip is attached to the bib and must be worn throughout the race. A bag-drop service is available for car keys and other belongings. After the race, hot soup and bread are served to all participants, while homemade baked goods and drinks are available for purchase. Medical staff will be on site. Parking is available near the event area, and the nearest public transport stop is Töpelsgatan. The courses are marked with fluorescent red tape and clear arrows at junctions. Runners are responsible for following the correct course at junctions. The event venue is IFK Göteborg Orienteering’s clubhouse in Skatås. There are youth categories and a kids’ trail race, aid stations and food after the finish; parking is free.

name: Highland Charity Backyard Ultra
organizer: Highland Trail Club och Höglandskyrkan i Sävsjö
description: Highland Charity Backyard Ultra is a welcoming race in the deepest forests of Småland, featuring a scenic, hilly 6.7 km backyard loop and a 3.7 km loop suitable for children and recreational runners. The event is organised by Highland Trail Club and Höglandskyrkan in Sävsjö, with a focus on community and charity; all proceeds go to charitable causes. The number of laps is limited to 15, creating a challenging but fun experience for all participants.
course_highlights: Hilly 6.7 km backyard loop through the forests of Småland
3.7 km loop suitable for children and recreational runners
Nature-focused race with a charitable purpose
additional: The race runs from Saturday at 09:00 to Sunday at 00:00. The number of laps is limited to 15. All proceeds from the race go to charitable causes. Backyard laps start on the hour. 09:00; information about the 2027 start time is unavailable.

name: Blue Mountain Trail Run
price_range: 150-450 kr beroende på distans och anmälningstid

price_tiers.distance: 15 km - Alvars stig by Nordväggen AB
6 km - Östra Ånnabodasjön by ICA Glansen

description:
Blue Mountain TrailRun is a trail race in Kilsbergen, 20 kilometres west of Örebro. There are four courses of 6, 10, 15 and 21 km, all starting and finishing at First Camp Ånnaboda.

The courses follow Bergslagsleden and the MTB trails around Ånnaboda: narrow trails, roots and rocks, boardwalks over streams, moss-covered spruce forest and views of forest lakes. The 21 km Blankhult course has 527 metres of elevation gain and is the race’s long loop for those looking for technical trails and hills. The 15 km Alvars stig is the middle-distance course, with trails all the way. The 10 km Trolldalsvägen is the classic 10-kilometre course. The 6 km Östra Ånnabodasjön course goes around the lake on mostly easy-running trails and is suitable as a first trail race.

Men’s and women’s categories on all courses, no time limit, electronic timing and a medal for everyone who finishes. The runner who breaks the course record on the 21 km course receives SEK 5,000. The fifth edition takes place in 2027. The race has been organised by Garphyttans IF Orientering since 2023.
course_highlights: Technical trails and hilly terrain along stage 9 of Bergslagsleden
Passes several forest lakes, including Norra Ånnabodasjön and Stora Dammsjön
Climb to Sånnabodahöjden, with sweeping views over Närkeslätten
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the race office from 09.00. Registration opens on 1 December 2026. The registration deadline is 22 May 2027. Late registration is available on race day from 09.00 to 09.15, subject to availability. Start times: 6 km at 09.43, 21 km at 10.00, 15 km at 10.35 and 10 km at 11.00. Aid stations with water, sports drink and snacks are located approximately every five kilometres. Trail shoes are recommended. Burgers, coffee and refreshments are available in the finish area. Swim in Södra Ånnabodasjön after the race. 21 km course records: 1:16:41 (men) and 1:29:16 (women).

name: Småland Adventure Race
description: A warm welcome to Småland Adventure Race 2027. After three fantastic years, we’re ready to take on a new challenge and aim for a race that’s at least as good as the last one. Småland Adventure Race is a multisport competition in which teams of 2–4 people use a map and compass to visit all checkpoints (CPs) as quickly as possible. CPs usually consist of a small physical orienteering marker and are marked with circles on the maps. The course will include a number of transition areas (TAs) where teams switch between disciplines. The race will mainly involve running, mountain biking and paddling, along with other adventures. In the three previous races, participants have paddled on air mattresses, climbed, tackled a high ropes course, gone SUPing and run a maze orienteering course. Some checkpoints have been at the top of climbing nets and others in the middle of a slackline, but most are in more accessible locations. We can promise many hours of wonderful adventure! We offer a long and a short class. Provisionally, teams in the long class will be out for 22–26 hours, and teams in the short class for 11–13 hours. In 2027, we’re also offering a Bike and Run class, a recreational class where you’ll be out for just 5–7 hours and take on a few fewer adventures—but still have a great time.
